[[File:Mainardi, Matteo – Opere, 1646 – BEIC IE7970797.jpg|thumb|''Opere mercantili et economiche'', 1646]]
'''Matteo Mainardi''' ([[Bologna]], late 16th century – after 1646) was an Italian [[economist]] and [[Arithmetics|arithmetician]].<ref name="Orlandi1714" />

== Life ==
Born in [[Bologna]], he is known for having done the history of the [[bookkeeping]] in Italy in the 17th century, along with [[Antonio Maria Villavecchia]], [[Ambrogio Lerici]], [[Giovanni Domenico Peri]], [[Simon Grisogono]], [[Giovanni Antonio Moschetti]], [[Lodovico Flori]], and others. He wrote many books about bookkeeping, and a history of the origin of every church in Bologna. All of his works were reprinted in 1700 in Bologna by Longhi.<ref name="Orlandi1714">{{cite book|author=Pellegrino Antonio Orlandi|title=Notizie degli scrittori bolognesi e dell'opere loro stampate e manoscritte|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jIXPAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA209|year=1714|publisher=C. Pisarri|pages=203, 209|language=it}}</ref> His 1632 work ''La scrittura mercantile formatamente regolata'' is considered particularly relevant.<ref name="Geijsbeek">{{cite book|author=J.B. Geijsbeek|title=Ancient Double-Entry Bookkeeping|url=https://archive.org/details/ancientdoubleent00geijuoft|year=1914|publisher=John B. Geijsbeek|location=Denver, Colorado|isbn=978-5-87431-394-4|pages=[https://archive.org/details/ancientdoubleent00geijuoft/page/107 107]–}}</ref>
